label: Metacognition and motivation
summary: Helping learners steer their own learning, planning, checking and judging what they know, inside the work at hand; and what holds up on motivation, growth mindset included.

items.text: Before they start, ask what the task wants, what they already know that could help, and how they will begin.

evidence.original: Metacognition has a strong average and is hard to realize. The EEF Toolkit puts it at +8 months across 355 studies, with a padlock lost because many were not independently evaluated, and warns the impact is hard to achieve in practice; its guidance recommends explicit teaching of planning, monitoring and evaluating within subject lessons, and modeling (EEF Toolkit, 2025; EEF, 2025). Two meta-analyses of 84 school studies found a mean of 0.69, larger when researchers rather than teachers delivered and in math (Dignath & Büttner, 2008). Study skills transfer best when trained in context (Hattie et al., 1996). College students who judged their recall more accurately retained more (Dunlosky & Rawson, 2012), and people often misjudge how they learn (Bjork et al., 2013). Rereading rates low and practice testing high (Dunlosky et al., 2013). Growth mindset, honestly: a meta-analysis of 63 studies found d = 0.05, not significant after correcting for bias, and 0.02 in the best studies (Macnamara & Burgoyne, 2023); another found d = 0.14 for targeted groups with high fidelity, with a prediction interval from -0.08 to 0.35 (Burnette et al., 2023). A national trial with 12,490 US ninth graders raised lower achievers' grades by 0.10 points, more where peer norms fitted, and not higher achievers' (Yeager et al., 2019). Earlier overall effects were weak (Sisk et al., 2018), and replication attempts of the praise-for-intelligence study with 624 children aged 9-13 in China were largely null (Li & Bates, 2019; Mueller & Dweck, 1998). So these lines don't teach mindset; they only avoid trait labels. Choice: 41 studies, raising motivation and effort, strongest for instructionally irrelevant choices (Patall et al., 2008). Relevance: one experiment in first-year high school science, largest for those low in confidence (Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009); motivation interventions overall d = 0.49, smaller in randomized designs (Lazowski & Hulleman, 2016).
evidence.unknown: Most of this is teachers in schools over weeks, not a model in a single chat. Whether a line or two of prompting about planning or confidence does anything is untested, and these prompts could become one more chore. Growth mindset messages from an AI have not been tested at scale here. AI help may also reduce a learner's own planning and checking (Fan et al., 2025; Darvishi et al., 2024): whether prompts like these offset that is not known.

risk_notes: Its text goes to a model as guidance. Nothing runs and nothing about a learner goes anywhere. What the teacher set for how far to go comes first. Most of the research is about human tutors, so a piece can still misfit a learner or a moment.
